(A) Axial T2-weighted image (T2WI) showing a mass measuring 20 cm in the right lower abdomen. The mass has increased in size with a higher proportion of solid components. The margin of the mass is disrupted on the left side, with protrusion of its contents at the disruption site (arrowhead). The mass demonstrates mildly high signal intensity with a low-signal-intensity rim (arrow). (B) Axial diffusion-weighted image (DWI) showing the mass with heterogeneous high signal intensity. A: Panel (a) is the patient's tumor stained for estrogen receptor; the in-text report describes intermediate ER positivity in a uterine leiomyosarcoma metastatic to the ovarian stroma. Tumor cells show spindle/ovoid morphology in fascicles consistent with the smooth-muscle neoplasm. B: Panel (b) is the progesterone receptor immunostain, described in the text as strongly positive, in the same uterine leiomyosarcoma metastatic to the ovary; fascicular spindle cell growth is visible. C: Panel (c) is the desmin immunostain, reported as strongly positive, confirming the smooth-muscle lineage of the uterine leiomyosarcoma deposits in the ovary. D: Panel (d) is the CD10 immunostain, described as weakly positive, of the same uterine leiomyosarcoma involving ovarian stroma; spindle cell fascicles are evident.
